newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BANKS REJECT STEELMAKER CLABECQ SALVAGE PLAN.
newsitem.headline: BANKS REJECT STEELMAKER CLABECQ SALVAGE PLAN.

text.p: A group of banks have rejected an interim salvage plan for bankrupt Belgian steelmaker Forges de Clabecq, throwing the future of the firm back into doubt, liquidator Alain Zenner told Belgia radio on Wednesday.
"The banks gave a negative answer last night," Zenner, beaten up by angry steelworkers two weeks ago, said.
Clabecq was declared bankrupt in January after the government of Belgium's French-speaking Walloon region pulled the plug.

The group of liquidators have been trying ever since to patch together a deal to keep the firm going for five months in order to fulfil a backlog of orders and try to find a buyer for the company as a going concern.
The workers for their part have taken legal action to try to force both the Walloon government and the creditor banks to come up with a rescue package.

The Walloon government, under pressure from the court, did agree to come up with 225 million francs ($6.6 million) but only on condition that the banks came up with the same amount -- an act they have now refused.
"The plan...proves it is not possible to keep the company running in a balanced manner," Zenner said. "There would still be a loss."
The court still has the last word, and Zenner said the liquidators would abide by that.
